newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds narrowly mixed on low volume.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds narrowly mixed on low volume.

text.p: Brady bond prices were narrowly mixed on extremely low volume on Tuesday as the absence of any fresh economic data kept potential buyers out of the market, emerging market debt traders said.
"I haven't seen one trade go through today. It has been very quiet," said one Brady bond trader at a U.S. investment bank in London.
Traders said activity in the emerging debt market was likely to remain thin ahead of a slew of key U.S. inflation reports due out next week.

The U.S. data, which could have a major impact on the direction of U.S. interest rates as well as other dollar instruments such as Bradys, includes July retail sales, producer prices and consumer prices.
"Next week's data will set the tone for where we are going though I think generally people aren't that worried as long as there is no wage inflation," the trader said.
In Eastern Europe, Russian Vnesheconombank dollar-denominated loans were 1/4 higher at 96-1/2 bid and the country's PRINs were 1/8 firmer at 70-5/8 bid.
Traders attributed the rise in Russian loans to expectations the country's debt restructuring agreement with commercial bank creditors will close by October.
In the Latin Brady market, prices were mostly lower in quiet trade.
Argentine FRBs were 1/4 weaker at 95-1/8 bid, Brazilian "C" bonds were unchanged at 83 bid and Mexican pars were 1/8 softer at 81 bid.
